incidents.title: Login with unknown email crashes
incidents.expected_cause: get_user_by_email returns None for an unknown email and authenticate reads user.password_hash without a None check
incidents.judge_reason: Candidate 1 explicitly states the None check was removed and that authenticate accesses user.password_hash when get_user_by_email returns None, matching the ground truth mechanism.

incidents.title: Signup crashes: query uses a column that does not exist
incidents.expected_cause: The query filters on User.username, but the User model has no such column; the column is called email
incidents.judge_reason: The candidate correctly identifies that the query uses User.username, which does not exist, and that the User model only has an email column, matching the ground truth.

incidents.title: Payment crashes: required environment variable is not set
incidents.expected_cause: create_payment reads the PAYMENT_API_KEY environment variable, which is not set in this environment
incidents.judge_reason: Candidate 1 explicitly states that create_payment reads PAYMENT_API_KEY via os.environ and the variable is not defined, matching the ground truth defect.
patch_warnings: demo_app/shop/payment_service.py: a required environment variable became optional, so a missing setting is no longer detected

incidents.title: Payment for a non-existent user fails with a database error
incidents.expected_cause: Foreign key enforcement was enabled in database.py, but create_payment never checks that the user exists, so a payment for a missing user violates the FOREIGN KEY constraint
incidents.judge_reason: None of the candidates explicitly state that create_payment lacks a user existence check, which is the specific defect identified in the ground truth.

incidents.title: Normal payments rejected after a bad configuration value
incidents.expected_cause: MAX_PAYMENT_AMOUNT was set to 10 in the latest release (previously 10000), so normal payments are rejected
incidents.judge_reason: The candidate correctly identifies the same defect: MAX_PAYMENT_AMOUNT was lowered to 10 in the latest release, causing normal payments to be rejected.

incidents.title: Signup times out waiting for a database connection
incidents.expected_cause: The connection pool was shrunk to one connection with no overflow, and record_signup_audit opens a second session while the request session still holds that connection, so the checkout times out
incidents.judge_reason: Candidate 1 explicitly mentions the pool size and overflow settings causing the timeout, matching the ground truth.

incidents.title: Signup fails: required package is not installed
incidents.expected_cause: hash_password imports argon2, but the package was never added to requirements.txt or installed in this environment
incidents.judge_reason: Candidate 1 correctly identifies the missing Argon2 dependency as the root cause, matching the ground truth.
patch_warnings: AI review: The patch replaces the missing argon2 dependency with a different hashing algorithm, altering functionality rather than restoring the original dependency.

incidents.title: Payment crashes: fee rate from config is a string
incidents.expected_cause: FEE_RATE is read with os.getenv, so it is a string, and create_payment multiplies the float amount by that string
incidents.judge_reason: Both diagnoses identify that FEE_RATE is a string not cast to float, causing a multiplication error.

incidents.title: Payment fails after saving: cannot write receipt file
incidents.expected_cause: create_payment writes receipts to /var/shop/receipts, a directory the application user is not allowed to create
incidents.judge_reason: Candidate 1 correctly identifies the same permission issue with writing to /var/shop/receipts as the ground truth.

incidents.title: Signup crashes for users with a one-word name
incidents.expected_cause: create_user takes name.split()[1], which assumes the name has at least two words, but the name was a single word
incidents.judge_reason: Candidate 1 correctly identifies the defect of assuming a two‑word name and using name.split()[1] on a single‑word input.

incidents.title: Payments fail: payment gateway refuses connections
incidents.expected_cause: create_payment calls the payment gateway at GATEWAY_URL, but nothing is listening on that address, so the connection is refused
incidents.judge_reason: Candidate 2 correctly identifies the service not listening on the expected port, matching the ground truth root cause.
patch_warnings: demo_app/shop/payment_service.py: the call to httpx.post(...) was removed, so the code no longer contacts that service

incidents.title: Signup crashes with maximum recursion depth exceeded
incidents.expected_cause: normalize_email calls itself instead of returning the cleaned value, so it recurses until the recursion limit
incidents.judge_reason: The candidate explicitly states that normalize_email calls itself recursively, causing infinite recursion, which is the same root cause described in the ground truth.

incidents.title: Every login crashes after password comparison change
incidents.expected_cause: authenticate calls .decode() on password_hash, which is already a str, so every login raises AttributeError
incidents.judge_reason: The candidate correctly identifies the same defect: a .decode() call on a string password_hash causing AttributeError.

incidents.title: Duplicate signup returns 500 with a unique constraint error
incidents.expected_cause: The email-exists check was removed from the signup route, so a duplicate email reaches the database and violates the UNIQUE constraint on users.email
incidents.judge_reason: Candidate 1 correctly identifies the removal of the email-existence check causing duplicate inserts that hit the UNIQUE constraint, matching the ground truth root cause.

incidents.title: Payment saved but request fails: raw SQL uses wrong table
incidents.expected_cause: The raw SQL query selects from a table named payment, but the table is called payments
incidents.judge_reason: Both state that the SQL query references the wrong table name, causing the SELECT to fail.
